GitHub user pavel-kuznetsov opened a pull request:

https://github.com/apache/ignite/pull/4976

IGNITE-9557: Assert in case of explains of updates operations.

You can merge this pull request into a Git repository by running:

$ git pull https://github.com/gridgain/apache-ignite ignite-9557

Alternatively you can review and apply these changes as the patch at:

https://github.com/apache/ignite/pull/4976.patch

To close this pull request, make a commit to your master/trunk branch
with (at least) the following in the commit message:

This closes #4976

commit c58911894be0581b799cc7012005d8930d49de06
Author: Pavel Kuznetsov <palmihal@...>
Date: 2018-10-11T12:13:49Z

ignite-9557: tests for EXPLAIN update queries.

commit 74d30f9241ddc3a424a3fd589c8c32bf1d2448cb
Author: Pavel Kuznetsov <palmihal@...>
Date: 2018-10-12T14:25:01Z

ignite-9557: Throw exception on EXPLAIN of update query.

Added assertion that query is not a EXPLAIN of update operation: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE. In this case we throw IgniteSqlException with code of unsupported operation.
We don't support explains of update operations yet. Added correct exception to be thrown in this case.
tledkov-gridgain Could you please take a look at the patch?

pkouznet, my comments:

  • please review my minor changes;
  • new test ExplainSelfTest is not added to any suites. Please add and re-run tests.

Thank you!
Also moved test to another package and added to IgniteCacheQuerySelfTestSuite2

Test run : https://ci.ignite.apache.org/viewQueued.html?itemId=2098497
Tests look good (javadoc is known issue), vozerov could you please take a look at the patch?
Merged master, additionally re-ran the Javadoc https://ci.ignite.apache.org/viewQueued.html?itemId=2106083

pkouznet, my comments:

  1. Tests should go through public API (IgniteCache.query()), not through internal
  2. Need to add tests for local queries
  3. Need to add tests for SqlQuery (local and non-local) - what kind of exception will be there? Need to ensure that it makes sense
  4. Need to add tests for JDBC thin driver and ensure that proper SQL STATE is passed there. As this is "unsupported operation", SqlStateCode.UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION should be passed to driver.

Updated PR.
